problem: Classical SLAM-then-plan navigation is purely geometric: it cannot use learned regularities of indoor layouts to guess about unobserved space, and it is brittle when the mapper fails, e.g. on RGB input or texture-less walls. Contemporary end-to-end deep RL/IL navigation policies are reactive or rely on unstructured LSTM memory. They were mostly tested in random mazes or in training scenes (Zhu et al.), so they cannot build a map or plan, and they generalize poorly to unseen buildings.
motivation: Humans and even rats navigate new places using 'cognitive maps' and common-sense priors, such as a hallway probably leading to another hallway or where chairs tend to be. The authors argue that mapping should be driven by what the planner needs, and that a spatial memory should support planning under partial observation. Keeping only the architectural prior of a metric top-down belief, and learning everything else end-to-end, lets the agent exploit layout statistics of real buildings. The mapper can then also tolerate imperfect maps.
key_idea: Build a differentiable egocentric multi-scale top-down latent belief map, warped by egomotion and updated by a CNN from each first-person frame, and feed it to a differentiable hierarchical value-iteration planner. Train the two jointly with DAgger, so the map emerges from the navigation objective without map supervision.
insight: Explicit spatial memory plus planning structure generalizes to unseen buildings much better than reactive or LSTM memory. Evidence: the 1-frame reactive agent reaches about 9 steps mean distance-to-goal on training scenes but about 17 on the test scenes. CMP also degrades less than the LSTM when trained on a single floor (SR 67.9 vs 58.9) or transferred from an internal Matterport dataset (61.1 vs 48.6). The ablations in Table A2 (SR@39 steps) show three things: (1) the learned, task-driven mapper beats an analytic depth-projection mapper (78.3 vs 62.9, depth input); (2) the VIN planner matters mainly for RGB (a shallow CNN planner gives 58.6 vs 62.5); (3) the multi-scale planner costs only slight accuracy versus single-scale (62.5/78.3 vs 63.0/79.5, RGB/depth) while being far cheaper. Readout probes show the latent map is spatial, predicts free space behind doorways, and separates hallway from room space, none of which a purely geometric map can do. A classical geometric pipeline with depth and perfect pose remains very strong (SPL 80.6 vs 73.1 for CMP). With RGB it collapses (SPL 15.9) while CMP keeps 59.6, which shows the value of learned mapping when geometry is hard to recover.
method: Egocentric latent mapper φ: an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 encoder (the depth model is initialized via cross-modal distillation) maps each first-person RGB or depth frame to image-space features. Fully connected layers convert them to a top-down egocentric layout, and residual up-convolutions produce a multi-scale, multi-channel map update f'_t plus a confidence c'_t.

Egomotion warping W: a backward flow field ρ(e_t), computed analytically from the known egomotion (p = R_θ(p'+t)), is applied with differentiable bilinear sampling (spatial-transformer style). This warps the previous belief f_{t-1} and confidence c_{t-1} into the current robot frame.

Confidence-weighted belief update U: f_t = (f_{t-1}c_{t-1} + f'_t c'_t)/(c_{t-1}+c'_t) and c_t = c_{t-1}+c'_t. This analytic update acts like a GRU update gate, and the accumulated confidence tells the planner which regions are unobserved.

Hierarchical value iteration network planner (extending Tamar et al. v1): value iteration is implemented as convolutions plus channel-wise max-pooling. It runs l iterations on a k-times downsampled map, then center-crops, upsamples and refines at finer scales. This covers goals up to l·2^k steps with only l·k iterations, and it plans over the partially observed belief and goal to output the next macro-action.

End-to-end training by online DAgger: shortest-path supervision on a precomputed directed grid graph is used, with scheduled sampling (inverse-sigmoid decay of the expert probability). There is no supervision on the map. Optimization uses Adam, 60K iterations, lr 1e-3 dropped 10x every 20K, weight decay 1e-4 and batch norm.

Task variants: in the geometric (PointGoal) task the goal is a relative offset in the robot frame. In the semantic (ObjectGoal) task the goal is a one-hot category (chair, door or table), and a separate learned stop predictor thresholded on the validation set is used for SPL.

Sim-to-real execution: a TurtleBot 2 runs the RGB policy. The macro-actions (rotate 90°, forward 40 cm) are executed by an iLQR feedback controller on Dubins-car dynamics, with state estimated from wheel encoders and IMU.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 image encoder (ImageNet-pretrained for RGB; depth ResNet-50 via cross-modal distillation) + learned egocentric mapper + hierarchical value-iteration-network planner, trained end-to-end
setting.training_data: Imitation (DAgger) on shortest-path expert trajectories sampled on S3DIS training areas (2 buildings; 4 S3DIS environments, test on area4 from a 3rd building). The '+6 MP3D Envs' variant adds 6 large Matterport3D buildings. Extra experiments use an internal Matterport dataset (27 train / 4 val / 10 test environments). ImageNet pretraining for RGB; RGB-D pairs rendered from training meshes for depth distillation.
setting.observation: single egocentric RGB image or depth image per step (separate models) + perfect egomotion + goal (relative offset for geometric task, one-hot category for semantic task)
setting.action_space: discrete macro-actions on a grid graph: stay-in-place, rotate left/right 90°, move forward 40 cm
setting.simulator: custom simulator rendering S3DIS (and Matterport3D / internal Matterport) mesh scans on a precomputed traversability graph
setting.privileged: perfect egomotion / odometry assumed in simulation (in the real robot, estimated from wheel encoders + IMU); no GT map at test time

numbers_note:
Custom S3DIS benchmark (pre-Habitat), so no canonical names apply. Distances are in grid steps (1 step = 40 cm), and SR (success within 3 steps) is reported at 39 and 199 steps. The main-text sentence ('improves the success rate to 62.5% and 78.3% from 53.0% and 71.8%') does not match Table 1, which shows CMP 63.0/78.8 and LSTM 52.1/71.3 at 39 steps. The 62.5/78.3 values appear as 'Full model' in ablation Table A2, probably from the CVPR version; table values were used here.

CMP rows on the classical-comparison subsets were omitted as separate entries:
- Geometric, 1000 episodes: RGB SR@39 63.0, SR@199 80.6, SPL 59.6; Depth SR@39 78.4, SR@199 88.7, SPL 73.1.
- Semantic RGB, 500 episodes: mean SR@39 28.4, SR@199 37.3, SPL 14.0.
- Semantic Depth, 1000 episodes: mean SR@39 42.2, SR@199 51.9, SPL 20.1.

Ablations (Table A2, geometric, SR@39, RGB/Depth): Single-scale 63.0/79.5, Shallow planner 58.6/79.0, Analytic map (depth only) 62.9.

Generalization (Table A3, depth, SR): Train on 1 floor CMP 67.9 vs LSTM 58.9; Transfer from internal Matterport CMP 61.1 vs LSTM 48.6.

Mapper unit test (Table A1, free-space AP): analytic projection 56.1; learned RGB 74.9; learned depth random-init 63.4; learned depth distillation-init 78.4.

Figure-only results: internal Matterport dataset (10 test envs), run-to-run variance, and hardness analysis.
results: On unseen S3DIS test buildings, CMP beats all learned baselines on the geometric task. At 199 steps it reaches SPL 59.4 (RGB) and 73.7 (depth), vs 51.3/69.1 for the LSTM agent and 17.4/52.0 for the 4-frame reactive agent. SR@39 is 63.0/78.8 vs LSTM 52.1/71.3. Against a classical geometric mapper+planner with perfect pose, CMP wins decisively on RGB (SPL 59.6 vs 15.9) but loses on depth (73.1 vs 80.6); adding 6 MP3D buildings lifts CMP to 70.8 (RGB) and 82.3 (depth). On the semantic ObjectGoal task, CMP roughly doubles LSTM mean success at 199 steps (40.5 vs 26.0 RGB; 51.0 vs 29.3 depth), though all SPLs stay low (13.6/19.8). The sim-trained RGB policy reaches 68% success on a real TurtleBot 2.
limitations: Assumes perfect odometry/egomotion in simulation. Grid-world macro-actions (90° turns, 40 cm steps) on a static environment, with a small testbed (one held-out S3DIS floor).
Metric multi-scale maps scale poorly to large environments, and coarse-scale planning is approximate and can lose connectivity.

DAgger imitation of a full-information shortest-path expert can demand actions infeasible under partial observability. This hurts the semantic task (low SPL), and a classical depth+pose pipeline still outperforms CMP-S3DIS on PointGoal SPL.
compares_to: Reactive policy (4 frames, Zhu et al.-style)
Classical geometric mapping + path planning (depth projection / COLMAP SfM)
